AGM: electrolyte in a glass mat, sealed, maintenance-free, 10–12 years in float mode at 20–25 °C, the most affordable option for UPS. OPzV: gel electrolyte and tubular positive plates, 15–18 years, resistant to deep discharge. OPzS: liquid electrolyte, up to 20 years, require topping up with water and a separate ventilated room, but handle cyclic duty best.

On-line (double conversion) constantly feeds the load through the rectifier and inverter, so the output voltage and frequency are always stable and the transfer to batteries takes 0 ms. Line-interactive passes the mains straight through, correcting it with an autotransformer, and switches to the inverter in 2–10 ms. For servers, healthcare and machine tools we use on-line only.

An STS transfers the critical load between two independent sources (two UPS, UPS and mains, two inputs) in less than 4 ms, i.e. imperceptibly for servers, medical and telecom equipment. Used in 2N schemes and for equipment with a single power supply that cannot be connected to two inputs directly.
